rationale: An active block-all takedown is the highest-precedence monotonic restriction.
The scoped takedown permits citation metadata only and suppresses every external locator.
Rights evidence does not permit a public external locator.
Provider policy is independently more restrictive than the rights assessment.
Unknown or incomplete rights may expose only an independently allowlisted healthy canonical record link.
Unknown or incomplete rights with no qualified canonical link remain citation only.
Unknown or incomplete provider policy cannot authorize any external locator.
The rights assessment caps delivery at an allowlisted canonical record link.
An unavailable or stale canonical link lowers delivery to citation only.
Provider policy disallows pixel embedding but permits an allowlisted healthy source viewer.
An unhealthy viewer can only lower delivery to a separately qualified canonical link.
Viewer-only policy with no qualified public locator is citation only.
Provider policy disallows embedding or permits links only despite broader rights evidence.
Link-only provider policy with no qualified canonical record is citation only.
Incomplete required attribution prevents remote pixels but may retain an allowlisted canonical link.
Incomplete required attribution and no qualified canonical link yields citation only.
Remote pixels are exposed only when rights and policy explicitly allow them, attribution is complete, and the selected typed pixel locator is healthy and fresh.
An unhealthy, stale, redirected, blocked, or missing pixel endpoint can only lower delivery to a separately qualified canonical link.
Positive rights and policy do not overcome the absence of a qualified public locator.
Any unregistered state or unmatched combination fails closed without inventing a permissive mapping.
